correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the point-line Levi graph using projective Pappus coordinates and checked its isomorphism with the signed-offset LCF graph. A direct crossing-edge scan of all 262144 subsets gave b=(0,3,4,5,6,7,6,7,8,7,8,7,6,7,6,5,4,3,0) and m=(1,18,27,54,126,324,18,108,540,54,540,108,18,324,126,54,27,18,1), including the empty and full sets. The LCF prefixes realize every entry of b. Each edge contributes its span to the sum of prefix cuts, so sum(b)=99 and max(b)=8 are attained lower bounds on the two objectives. Equality for the sum holds exactly when all prefixes are minimizing sets. With one path at the empty set, forward extension by one vertex to any minimizing superset counts each labelled optimal order once and gives 31,850,496 paths to the full set. No identification by automorphisms or reversal was taken. Replay and raw results: /workspace/review-evidence/1/pappus_independent_check.py and /workspace/review-evidence/1/pappus_independent_check.out. The frozen certificate and checkers were inspected, not executed.

No priority inference is drawn from their same-day dates.

value.rationale: For a canonical small cubic symmetric incidence graph, the complete minimizer tie counts and the precise number of labelled optimum layouts quantify the degeneracy of two linked optimization problems, beyond a best-known objective and beyond existence of a nested order. They provide a reproducible exact benchmark for subset and layout enumeration methods with unambiguous symmetry normalization. The result need not assert generalization to other configurations or other Hamilton cycles to supply those invariants.
